Dashboard Review, Round Two

7 Oct 2026, desktop at 1440px. The review drew on five skills (design critique, data visualisation, Refactoring UI, Apple design principles, LLM Council) and 48 published standards. Every "After" here is a mock-up made in the browser; no code has changed for any of them. Nothing is built until you approve. Then: code first, then Figma.

Council Verdict: the ten suggestions, pressure-tested

Where the council agrees

  • The biggest risk was not on my list. Four of six programmes show mock values, and today a public visitor sees no mark on any of them. The mark exists but is switched off.
  • Allocation and expenditure belong in one chart, with budgeted, revised and spent side by side for each year. Modelled years must look different from published ones.
  • Drop item 5 (SHRESHTA's figures in the banner). It repeats the tiles directly below.
  • Ship 6, 7, 8 and 9. They fix charts that mislead. Items 1–4 are safe polish.

Where the council clashes

  • The dual-axis charts. The Executor would keep them because you asked for them. The Contrarian, First Principles and Outsider say the crossing of the line and the bars is invented by how the two scales are set, and readers will read meaning into it. Two aligned panels in one card satisfy both sides.
  • Scope. The Expansionist wants new features: pick a state for every card, CSV download, change-since-last-year in the hero. The other four say fix trust first. All five reviewers agreed with them.

Blind spots the council caught

  • Item 10's colours were backwards. The DAPSC mandate is a minimum, so colour must show compliance, not whether the difference is plus or minus.
  • The hero is real but unclear. 34.84 Cr counts people reached by NMBA awareness activities, not beneficiaries, and it doesn't say so.
  • Every figure needs a source and an "as on" date beside it, and a filter must change every figure or say which ones it leaves alone.

The recommendation

Fix trust first: show the Illustrative mark by default, clarify the hero, and redraw the DAPSC funds as one chart. Then restructure the landing page so the overview fits in half its current length. Then the chart fixes, then the polish. Retire the dual axis in favour of two aligned panels, but only once you agree, because it reverses your request.

The one thing to do first

Decide whether "Illustrative" shows by default on the public page. Everything else depends on readers being able to tell real from mock.

In plain English

I asked five reviewers, each with a different job: one hunting for flaws, one asking what the page is for, one looking for bigger wins, one reading as an ordinary citizen, and one asking what can be done on Monday. They agreed that most of my earlier suggestions are sound tidying. But the most important problem was missing from my list: the page shows made-up placeholder numbers next to real ones, with nothing to tell them apart. Picture a shop with real and display-only price tags that look identical. The first fix is to label the placeholder numbers where everyone can see them. Then come the shorter page, the clearer charts and the polish.

Raised by the critique and standards, not mocked up in this round

  • Spell out acronyms on first use (NMBA, DAPSC, SHRESHTA, SHREYAS, B.E., R.E.). The sheet's labels stay; the full name goes in the subtitle.
  • One number format per figure: compact in tiles and the hero, with the full figure on hover and in the table.
  • A "Showing: All India · All applicants" line, plus a statement wherever a card does not respond to a filter.
  • Change since last year on the hero figures, only where both years are real.
  • Coloured figures (green NMBA, orange SMILE, gold SCW): colour sits on the card edge and the figures stay in ink, so the page stays colourful while the numbers stop varying in colour for no reason. Not mocked up, because you asked for a colourful page; your call.

1 · Fix before the Department sees it

The data must be honest before any polish counts. All five advisors and all five reviewers put this first.

Your decisionDashboard overview › Dashboards by Portal

Show the 'Illustrative' mark by default

Today a public visitor sees no mark on any mock figure. The mark exists on every card but is hidden by an earlier product decision. With it on, the reader sees 'Live' on NMBA's real figures and 'Illustrative' beside each mock one, inside the card, so the mark stays in a cropped screenshot. This reverses your earlier decision, so it needs your yes.

Your decisionSMILE › Coverage and Outreach

The same mark on programme pages

Each mock tile carries the word beside its number. Every NMBA figure carries 'Live'.

RecommendedDashboard overview › hero

The headline figure says what it counts

'34.84 Cr Total Outreach' is real (NMBA's live feed), but it doesn't say what it counts. A reader can take it for 34 crore beneficiaries, a quarter of India. The label stays as in the sheet; the line under it says it counts people reached by awareness activities, since launch, and gives the as-on date. 'Share of Fund Release' under ₹67,977 Cr was a chart's name, not a description, so it now gives the schemes and years.

2 · Your two questions

RecommendedYear by Year Trends

SC / OBC / SHREYAS as a segmented button

SAMAVESH's segmented button is the ButtonGroup with segments attached: the selected segment is filled and the others are outlined, with aria-pressed. It reads as a choice of view, not as tabs. The rest of the dashboard uses the same pill control in four places (state map, theme chips stay chips); the build swaps every instance.

RecommendedDAPSC › Funds

DAPSC: allocation and expenditure in one chart

Your question: is one expenditure value right? Yes. B.E. and R.E. are the two estimates of the allocation: budgeted, then revised in mid-year. Expenditure is what was actually spent, so it has one figure a year. The sheet's name 'Total DAPSC Expenditure (B.E. and R.E.)' most likely means expenditure against B.E. and R.E., so I've noted it for the Department to correct. Two cards made the reader compare across a gap; one chart puts budgeted, revised and spent side by side for each year. Published figures are solid: every B.E. from the Union Budget, R.E. 2025-26 and the 2024-25 actual. Modelled ones are hatched and say so. 2026-27 has no R.E. yet and shows spending only to September. This also removes the empty dashed stub of earlier item 10.

3 · Structure: overview first, details one click down

Shneiderman's 'overview first, zoom and filter, details on demand', and your own rule that the landing page holds Department and Portal cards and the detail sits inside.

RecommendedDashboard overview

The landing page: hero, programmes, States/UTs

Today, 60% of the landing page is the education schemes' detail: Scholarships, Hostels, Year by Year Trends and Year on Year Report, about 2,900px before the portals appear. Here that detail moves to its own page behind one Department card, and the landing page drops from about 5,400px to about 2,970px. Six programme cards sit in three even rows (5+7, 6+6, 6+6), so no card stands alone. Every figure on the new card is the Department's own, as on the page today. Nothing is removed; it moves one click down.

RecommendedEducation page (today's landing)

Inside the education page: one 'Year by Year Trends' section

'Year by Year Trends' followed by 'Year on Year Report' gives two headings for one idea. The three year-wise charts become its second row.

Your decisionYear on Year Report

Year-wise count and funds: two aligned panels in one card

This goes against your earlier request. You asked for count and fund in one chart, so today two scales share one plot: Seats 0–4,000 against ₹ Cr 0–50. Where the line crosses a bar depends only on how the two axes were scaled, yet readers take the crossing as meaningful. ONS, the UK Analysis Function and Stephen Few all advise against dual axes. This keeps your 'one card' and the shared years, but gives counts and funds a panel each, with the latest value at the top right.

4 · Charts that say the wrong thing

RecommendedEducation

Share of Fund Release: ranked bars, not a 9-slice donut

One slice is 69% and six are under 2%. Guidance caps a donut at five slices; sorted bars show every scheme, its amount and its share.

RecommendedSMILE › Skill & Training

Status breakdowns use status colours

'Completed' in red reads as failed. Completed is green, In Progress blue, Discontinued grey. Red as the palette's second colour site-wide is a SAMAVESH change; it is recorded, not made here.

RecommendedState/UT-wise Figures

Lowest five States/UTs: rank and value, no empty bars

On the national scale the lowest five draw 1px bars that look broken. They are real NMBA figures, not missing data, so they keep their value and '32 of 36'.

Recommended (replaces item 10)DAPSC › Mandated Allocation

Mandated Allocation: judged against the mandate

Item 10 coloured the difference by its sign. The mandate is a minimum, so the colour must follow compliance: 'Meets, +0.8 pp' with a tick in green, 'Short by 0.7 pp' with a warning sign in amber, not red. The words and icon carry the meaning without the colour. The figures are illustrative.
